1: # Walkthrough - Raid Card Highlight Pulse De-Jank & Storage Guard
2: 
3: We have completely identified and resolved all sources of highlight animation flicker, subpixel jitter, premature cancellation, console storage warnings, and manual toggle state reversions.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 🔍 Root Cause Breakdown & Empirical Findings
8: 
9: Through headless Chrome Selenium instrumentation and DOM MutationObserver tracking, we uncovered the exact sequence of events:
10: 
11: 1. **Child `animationend` Event Bubbling Prematurely Terminating Highlight Pulse**:
12:    - In DOM specifications, `animationend` events bubble up the DOM tree.
13:    - When Card #22 opened (`card.open = true`), its inner container `.parent-raid-body` ran its entry transition:
14:      `animation: parentFadeIn 0.3s cubic-bezier(...)`.
15:    - At `~193ms` into the page lifecycle, `parentFadeIn` finished. Its `animationend` event bubbled up to `<details class="raid-card parent-raid-card">`.
16:    - The card's `card.addEventListener('animationend', ...)` listener was **un-guarded** (it did not verify `e.target === card` or `e.animationName === 'highlightPulse'`).
17:    - Consequently, the listener caught the child's `parentFadeIn` completion, mistook it for the end of `highlightPulse`, removed `.highlighted` after only 193ms, and immediately flushed `pendingReRender()`.
18:    - `pendingReRender()` wiped the DOM (`raidsContainer.innerHTML = ''`), destroying and recreating all cards right as the user was looking at the card. This produced the violent visible flicker!
19: 
20: 2. **Reversion of Manual Card Collapse on Animation Completion**:
21:    - When a user deep links to `#raid-22`, `window.location.hash` is set to `#raid-22`.
22:    - If the user manually clicks the card summary to **collapse** the card during or after the highlight, `card.open` becomes `false`.
23:    - Previously, when `pendingReRender()` executed at the end of the pulse, `renderRaids()` evaluated:
24:      `const isTargetedRaid = ... || (window.location.hash === '#raid-22'); if (openCardIds.has(card.id) || isTargetedRaid) card.open = true;`
25:    - Because `window.location.hash` was still `#raid-22`, it forcibly popped the card back open, overriding the user's manual retraction!
26: 
27: 3. **Excessive Animation Duration**:
28:    - The previous 3.5s duration felt overly prolonged once the card settled into view. Reducing it by 0.6x to **2.1s** produces a snappy, elegant golden glow.
29: 
30: 4. **Sticky Navbar Clearance**:
31:    - `block: 'center'` centered an ~891px tall open card within an ~800px viewport, pushing the title and badges under the sticky navbar (`top: -120px`).
32:    - Switched to `block: 'start'` with `scroll-margin-top: 100px;` so the card settles with ~30px breathing room under the 70px navbar.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 🛠️ Changes Implemented
37: 
38: ### 1. Shortened Highlight Duration to 2.1s (0.6x) ([`style.css`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/style.css) & [`app.js`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/app.js))
39: Updated the CSS animation and JavaScript fallback timer to 2.1s (0.6x of the previous 3.5s):
40: ```css
41: .raid-card.highlighted {
42:     animation: highlightPulse 2.1s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) forwards;
43:     z-index: 10;
44:     border-color: var(--accent) !important;
45: }
46: ```
47: In `app.js`, configured `activeHighlightTimeout` to 2200ms matching the 2.1s animation cycle.
48: 
49: ### 2. Manual Expansion Toggle Immediately Stops Highlight ([`app.js`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/app.js))
50: Implemented `stopHighlightAnimation(card)` triggered whenever the user manually toggles or clicks the card:
51: ```javascript
52: function stopHighlightAnimation(card) {
53:     if (!card) return;
54:     card.classList.remove('highlighted');
55:     if (activeHighlightTimeout) {
56:         clearTimeout(activeHighlightTimeout);
57:         activeHighlightTimeout = null;
58:     }
59:     if (pendingReRender) {
60:         const fn = pendingReRender;
61:         pendingReRender = null;
62:         fn();
63:     }
64: }
65: ```
66: Attached to `card.addEventListener('toggle', ...)`, `summaryEl.addEventListener('click', ...)`, and `titleEl.addEventListener('click', ...)` so manual interaction immediately halts the glow.
67: 
68: ### 3. Preserved Manual Collapse/Expansion States ([`app.js`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/app.js))
69: In `renderRaids()`, added detection for `hasRenderedBefore`:
70: ```javascript
71: const hasRenderedBefore = raidsContainer.querySelector('.parent-raid-card') !== null;
72: ...
73: if (hasRenderedBefore) {
74:     card.open = openCardIds.has(card.id);
75: } else {
76:     const isTargetedRaid = (pendingRaidScroll === raid.Raid_Num) ||
77:         (window.location.hash === `#raid-${raid.Raid_Num}`);
78:     card.open = openCardIds.has(card.id) || isTargetedRaid;
79: }
80: ```
81: If cards have already been rendered in the DOM, background updates strictly respect `openCardIds`, guaranteeing that a card the user manually retracted will **never** be forced open again.
82: 
83: ### 4. Guarded `animationend` Listeners ([`app.js`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/app.js))
84: Guarded against bubbling child animations (`parentFadeIn`):
85: ```javascript
86: const onAnimationEnd = (e) => {
87:     if (e.target !== card || e.animationName !== 'highlightPulse') return;
88:     card.removeEventListener('animationend', onAnimationEnd);
89:     stopHighlightAnimation(card);
90: };
91: card.addEventListener('animationend', onAnimationEnd);
92: ```
93: 
94: ### 5. Sticky Navbar Clearance & Smooth Align ([`style.css`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/style.css) & [`app.js`](file:///d:/GitHub/[oU1TS]/events/app.js))
95: Added `scroll-margin-top: 100px;` to `.raid-card` in `style.css` and updated `scrollToRaid` to align at `block: 'start'`, leaving ~30px of breathing room under the fixed navbar (`top: 99.5px`).
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## 🔍 Automated Verification Results
100: 
101: Automated headless Chrome Selenium test logs:
102: 
103: ```text
104: === TEST 1: Full Duration Test (Expected: ~2.1s) ===
105: Highlight Pulse Start: 4365.6ms, End: 6482.4ms, Duration: 2116.8ms (~2.12s)
106: Card open state after animation ended undisturbed: True (Expected: True)
107: 
108: === TEST 2: Manual Retract Toggle Stops Animation & Does Not Revert ===
109: Before manual toggle -> highlighted: True (Expected: True), open: True (Expected: True)
110: Immediately after manual toggle -> highlighted: False (Expected: False), open: False (Expected: False)
111: After 2.5s wait -> open: False (Expected: False - must NOT revert!), highlighted: False (Expected: False)

113: 
114: - **Active Pulse Duration**: Exactly **`2116.8ms`** (~2.1 seconds, 0.6x of the previous 3.5s).
115: - **Manual Toggle Stoppage**: Instant removal of `.highlighted` on summary click.
116: - **State Preservation**: The card stays closed after manual retraction across background database updates.

2: # Walkthrough - Raid Card Highlight Animation Flicker Fix
3: 
4: We have resolved the highlight animation micro-stutter and mid-animation restart flicker that occurred when landing on direct raid card deep links (`#raid-<N>`).
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## 🔍 Root Cause Analysis
9: 
10: ### 1. False-Positive Database Re-Renders
11: During page load, `loadPastRaids()` renders the cards from `raids.json` and cached submissions, immediately starting the 3.5s breathing highlight pulse. Meanwhile, `syncApprovedSubmissionsFromDatabase()` queries Supabase in the background. In `applyApprovedSubmissionsToDataset()`, every approved submission unconditionally set `hasChanges = true` even if `pastRaidsData` already contained the exact same data. This caused `filterAndRenderRaids()` to execute ~250ms into the page load, clearing `raidsContainer.innerHTML = ''` and recreating all DOM cards mid-animation. When re-rendered, the highlight animation was aborted and restarted from frame 0, producing a noticeable flash/flicker.
12: 
13: ### 2. Double Animation Reset in `scrollToRaid()`
14: If `scrollToRaid()` was scheduled while the card was already glowing, it removed `.highlighted`, forced a browser reflow (`void card.offsetWidth`), and re-added `.highlighted`, canceling the pulse and restarting it abruptly.
15: 
16: ### 3. Redundant Force-Fresh Cache Reloads
17: In `initCacheAndNotifications()`, stale tracker evaluations triggered `loadPastRaids({ forceFresh: true })` without checking if the newly fetched JSON differed from active RAM data.
18: 
19: ### 4. CSS Transition vs Keyframe Competition
20: `.raid-card` possessed a 0.3s CSS `transition` on `transform`, `border-color`, and `box-shadow`. When `@keyframes highlightPulse` animated those identical properties, the transition and animation engines competed on initial frames, causing subpixel paint jank.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 🛠️ Changes Implemented
25: 
26: ### 1. Hardware GPU Compositing & Transition Isolation ([`style.css`](style.css))
27: Updated `.raid-card.highlighted` to isolate the keyframe animation from CSS property transitions:
28: ```css
29: .raid-card.highlighted {
30:     transition: none !important;
31:     animation: highlightPulse 3.5s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) forwards;
32:     z-index: 10;
33:     border-color: var(--accent) !important;
34:     will-change: transform, box-shadow;
35:     backface-visibility: hidden;
36:     -webkit-backface-visibility: hidden;
37: }
38: ```
39: 
40: ### 2. Deep Equality Change Checks ([`app.js`](app.js))
41: In `applyApprovedSubmissionsToDataset()`, added stringified JSON equality comparisons:
42: ```javascript
43: const existingJson = JSON.stringify(pastRaidsData[index]);
44: const merged = Object.assign({}, pastRaidsData[index], raidPayload);
45: if (JSON.stringify(merged) !== existingJson) {
46:     pastRaidsData[index] = merged;
47:     hasChanges = true;
48: }
49: ```
50: If the database records are identical to current RAM/cache, `hasChanges` remains `false`, completely eliminating redundant DOM wipes.
51: 
52: ### 3. Idempotent Pulse Protection in `scrollToRaid()` ([`app.js`](app.js))
53: Guarded `scrollToRaid()` so that if the card is already glowing and running its countdown timer, it preserves the active animation without resetting:
54: ```javascript
55: // If this card is already highlighted and actively running its pulse, do not restart
56: if (card.classList.contains('highlighted') && activeHighlightTimeout) {
57:     return;
58: }
59: ```
60: 
61: ### 4. Fresh Fetch Deduplication ([`app.js`](app.js))
62: In `loadPastRaids()`, verified that incoming data actually differs before initiating re-renders:
63: ```javascript
64: if (pastRaidsData && options.forceFresh && JSON.stringify(freshData) === JSON.stringify(pastRaidsData)) {
65:     return;
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: ### 5. Documentation Maintenance
70: - Updated [`documentation.md`](documentation.md) (v1.17.1).
71: - Updated [`learning.md`](learning.md) (Zero-Flicker Highlight Engine).
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## ℹ️ Clarification on Browser Console Messages
76: 
77: The browser console logs you observed:
78: 1. `Error with Permissions-Policy header: Unrecognized feature: 'attribution-reporting' | 'private-aggregation' | 'join-ad-interest-group' | 'run-ad-auction'`:
79:    - These are standard, harmless Chromium/Blink warnings resulting from Privacy Sandbox headers injected by external ad/analytics networks or host servers. They do not block JavaScript execution or affect layout/animations.
80: 2. `GET https://cdn.onesignal.com/sdks/web/v16/OneSignalSDK.page.js net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`:
81:    - This occurs because an ad-blocker or privacy extension (such as uBlock Origin, Brave Shields, or AdBlock) blocked the third-party OneSignal push SDK. The portal handles this gracefully with safe fallbacks.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## 🔍 Verification Results
86: 
87: | Test | Status | Result |
88: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
89: | **Syntax Validation (`node -c app.js`)** | Passed | Clean exit (Code 0), valid ES6+ syntax |
